entries.name: Affine-Invariant Calibrated Covariance Estimation and Heavy-Tailed Ridge Regression
aliases: Calibrated Heavy-Tailed Covariance Estimation via Dyadic Regularization Halving (Ostrovskii & Rudi 2019)
Heavy-Tailed Ridge Regression via Calibrated Covariance Preconditioning
entries.definition: Affine-Invariant Calibrated Covariance Estimation and Heavy-Tailed Ridge Regression is a non-asymptotic statistical estimation and regression methodology introduced by Ostrovskii and Rudi (2019, COLT PMLR 99:2531-2550, arXiv:1902.03086v2) for estimating a population second-moment matrix S = E[X otimes X] in R^{d x d} from n independent copies of a heavy-tailed random vector X satisfying the directional fourth-moment kurtosis condition E^{1/4}[<X, u>^4] <= kappa E^{1/2}[<X, u>^2] for all u in R^d (Condition HT). Given a target regularization parameter lambda > 0 and regularized covariance S_lambda := S + lambda I_d, the methodology seeks a calibrated covariance estimate S_hat satisfying the affine-invariant relative Loewner-order approximation (1 - varepsilon) S_lambda <= S_hat_lambda <= (1 + varepsilon) S_lambda, equivalently ||S_lambda^{-1/2}(S_hat - S)S_lambda^{-1/2}|| <= varepsilon, with error governed by the effective degrees of freedom df_lambda(S) := Tr(S S_lambda^{-1}) <= min{rank(S), Tr(S)/lambda} rather than ambient dimension d. Whereas standard norm-clipped estimators S_hat^WM = (1/n) sum_{i=1}^n rho_theta(||X_i||) X_i otimes X_i with rho_theta(x) = psi_theta(x^2)/x^2 break affine equivariance and fail to achieve calibrated accuracy when lambda << ||S||, Algorithm 1 approximates the unobservable oracle estimator S_hat^o = (1/n) sum_{i=1}^n rho_theta(||S_lambda^{-1/2} X_i||) X_i otimes X_i through a multi-stage dyadic regularization halving scheme: starting from lambda_0 = L >= ||S|| across T = ceil(log_2(L/lambda)) halving steps (lambda_{t+1} = lambda_t / 2, q = T + 1) on disjoint sample-split batches of size m = floor(n / (2(T + 1))), it computes Cholesky factors R_t = Cholesky(S_hat_{lambda_t}^{(t)}) and reweights batch t+1 by alpha_i^{(t+1)} = rho_theta(||R_t^{-1} X_i^{(t+1)}||), followed by a final refinement on the remaining r >= n/2 samples in O(d^2 n + d^3 log(L/lambda)) time and O(d^2) space. Theorem 7 and Corollary 8 establish that for n >= 96^2 kappa^4 q df_lambda(S) log(4 q d/delta), S_hat achieves ||S_lambda^{-1/2}(S_hat - S)S_lambda^{-1/2}|| <= 48 kappa^2 sqrt(df_lambda(S) log(4d/delta) / n); Algorithm 2 and Theorem 10 combine Algorithm 1 with Lepskii's adaptive grid search over truncation levels theta_j = 2^j theta_min to adapt to unknown kappa and df_lambda(S); and Section 6 (Corollary 12 and Theorem 13) yields relative eigenvalue guarantees and optimal O(df_lambda(S) log(d/delta)/n + lambda^2 ||S_lambda^{-1/2} w^*||^2) excess risk for heavy-tailed ridge regression.

claims.statement: Under the fourth-moment kurtosis assumption Condition (HT) (E^{1/4}[<X, u>^4] <= kappa E^{1/2}[<X, u>^2] for all u in R^d), calibrated covariance estimation requires (1 - varepsilon) S_lambda <= S_hat_lambda <= (1 + varepsilon) S_lambda, equivalently ||S_lambda^{-1/2}(S_hat - S)S_lambda^{-1/2}|| <= varepsilon, which simultaneously guarantees entrywise variance recovery (1 - varepsilon) S_{ii} <= S_hat_{ii} <= (1 + varepsilon) S_{ii} when lambda <= min_i S_{ii} and directional variance control uniformly over u in R^d with complexity governed by the effective degrees of freedom df_lambda(S) := Tr(S S_lambda^{-1}) <= min{rank(S), Tr(S)/lambda}. Standard norm-truncated covariance estimators S_hat^WM = (1/n) sum_{i=1}^n rho_theta(||X_i||) X_i otimes X_i (Wei & Minsker 2017, Equations 6-8) achieve operator-norm error ||S_hat^WM - S|| = O(kappa^2 sqrt(||S|| Tr(S) log(d/delta) / n)), which provides calibrated guarantees only for lambda >= ||S|| because non-linear truncation of ||X_i|| breaks affine equivariance; whereas the idealized affine-invariant oracle estimator S_hat^o = (1/n) sum_{i=1}^n rho_theta(||S_lambda^{-1/2} X_i||) X_i otimes X_i achieves ||S_lambda^{-1/2}(S_hat^o - S)S_lambda^{-1/2}|| <= 6 kappa^2 sqrt(df_lambda(S) log(2d/delta) / n) for all lambda > 0 (Equations 10-13) since E[||S_lambda^{-1/2} X||^2 (S_lambda^{-1/2} X otimes S_lambda^{-1/2} X)] <= kappa^4 Tr(S S_lambda^{-1}) S_lambda^{-1/2} S S_lambda^{-1/2} <= kappa^4 df_lambda(S) I_d.

evidence.locator: Section 1, pp. 1-3, Condition (HT), Equations (1)-(5); Section 2.3, pp. 4-6, Lemma 5, Equations (6)-(13)

claims.statement: Lemma 14 establishes the dyadic effective-dimension doubling property df_{lambda/2}(S) <= 2 df_lambda(S) for any positive semidefinite matrix S and lambda > 0. Lemma 6 proves that if a preliminary estimate S_hat satisfies ||S_lambda^{-1/2}(S_hat - S)S_lambda^{-1/2}|| <= 1/2 (Event E), then (2/3) I_d <= S_lambda^{1/2} S_hat_lambda^{-1} S_lambda^{1/2} <= 2 I_d (Equation 35), |Tr(S S_hat_lambda^{-1}) - df_lambda(S)| <= 3 df_lambda(S) (Equation 37), and reweighting an independent sample X_1^+,...,X_m^+ via S_hat^{(+)} = (1/m) sum_{i=1}^m rho_theta(||S_hat_lambda^{-1/2} X_i^+||) X_i^+ otimes X_i^+ achieves calibrated accuracy at the halved regularization scale lambda/2: ||S_{lambda/2}^{-1/2}(S_hat^{(+)} - S)S_{lambda/2}^{-1/2}|| <= 6 theta log(2d/delta) / m with probability at least 1 - delta for theta >= 2 kappa^2 sqrt(m df_lambda(S) / log(2d/delta)) (Equations 16-17, Appendix B pp. 15-16). Algorithm 1 iterates this halving step across T = ceil(log_2(L/lambda)) stages (q = T + 1) on disjoint batches of size m = floor(n / (2(T + 1))) using Cholesky factors R_t = Cholesky(S_hat_{lambda_t}^{(t)}) in O(d^2 n + d^3 log(L/lambda)) time and O(d^2) space, and Theorem 7 and Corollary 8 prove that for theta = theta_* := 2 kappa^2 sqrt(n df_lambda(S) / (q log(4 q d/delta))) and n >= 96^2 kappa^4 q df_lambda(S) log(4 q d/delta), the final refined estimator S_hat satisfies ||S_lambda^{-1/2}(S_hat - S)S_lambda^{-1/2}|| <= 48 kappa^2 sqrt(df_lambda(S) log(4d/delta) / n) with probability at least 1 - delta.

evidence.locator: Sections 3-4, pp. 6-10, Algorithm 1, Lemma 6, Theorem 7, Corollary 8, Remark 9, Equations (15)-(26); Appendices A-B, pp. 15-16, Lemma 14, Equations (35)-(38)

claims.statement: To eliminate the dependence of the optimal truncation threshold theta_* on the unknown kurtosis parameter kappa and effective dimension df_lambda(S), Algorithm 2 (Section 5) runs Algorithm 1 over a geometric grid of candidate thresholds theta_j = 2^j theta_min for j in J = {0, 1, ..., ceil(log_2(theta_max / theta_min))} with theta_min = 2 sqrt(n / (q log(4 q d / delta))) and candidate error radii varepsilon_j = 12 theta_j log(4d/delta) / n, and selects the smallest index j_hat in J such that every finer candidate j' in J with j' >= j_hat satisfies the empirical calibrated compatibility condition ||S_hat_{j',lambda}^{-1/2}(S_hat_{j'} - S_hat_{j_hat})S_hat_{j',lambda}^{-1/2}|| <= 2(varepsilon_{j'} + varepsilon_{j_hat}) (Equation 28). Theorem 10 and Corollary 11 (Appendix C, pp. 16-17, Equations 39-43) prove that whenever theta_* in [theta_min, theta_max] and n >= 192^2 kappa^4 q df_lambda(S) log(4 q d |J| / delta), the selected estimator S_hat_{j_hat} achieves ||S_lambda^{-1/2}(S_hat_{j_hat} - S)S_lambda^{-1/2}|| <= 720 kappa^2 sqrt((1 + rho) df_lambda(S) log(4 d |J| / delta) / n) with probability at least 1 - delta in total time O(|J|(d^2 n + d^3 log(L/lambda))).

evidence.locator: Section 5, pp. 10-11, Algorithm 2, Theorem 10, Corollary 11, Equations (27)-(30); Appendix C, pp. 16-17, Equations (39)-(43)

claims.statement: As a consequence of calibrated covariance estimation, Corollary 12 (Section 6.1) shows via the Courant-Fischer minimax characterization that ||S_lambda^{-1/2}(S_hat - S)S_lambda^{-1/2}|| <= varepsilon implies relative eigenvalue bounds (1 - varepsilon) lambda_i - varepsilon lambda <= lambda_hat_i <= (1 + varepsilon) lambda_i + varepsilon lambda for all i in {1,...,d}, and hence (1 - 2 varepsilon) lambda_i <= lambda_hat_i <= (1 + 2 varepsilon) lambda_i for every eigenvalue lambda_i >= lambda. In heavy-tailed random-design linear regression (Section 6.2, Theorem 13, Appendix D pp. 17-20) where w^* = argmin_{w in R^d} L(w) with L(w) = E[(<X, w> - Y)^2], v^2 := L(w^*), and E[(<X, w^*> - Y)^4] <= varkappa^4 v^4, constructing S_hat via Algorithm 1 on a hold-out half X_{n+1},...,X_{2n} and forming the truncated pseudo-decorrelated response vector Z_bar = (1/n) sum_{i=1}^n rho_{theta_bar}(||Z_hat_i||^{1/2}) Z_hat_i with Z_hat_i = S_hat_lambda^{-1/2} X_i Y_i and theta_bar = 2 sqrt(6) kappa varkappa v sqrt(n df_lambda(S) / log(2d/delta)) yields the ridge estimator w_bar_lambda = S_hat_lambda^{-1/2} Z_bar satisfying L(w_bar_lambda) - L(w^*) <= O(1) ((kappa^4 + kappa^2 varkappa^2) v^2 df_lambda(S) log(2d/delta) / n + lambda^2 ||S_lambda^{-1/2} w^*||^2) whenever n >= C kappa^4 log(L/lambda) df_lambda(S) log(2d log(L/lambda) / delta) (Equation 34).

aio_mappings.rationale: AIO:RidgeRegression represents L2-regularized linear regression broadly, whereas Section 6.2 (Theorem 13) of AIMech:AffineInvariantCalibratedCovarianceEstimationAndHeavyTailedRidgeRegression constructs a heavy-tailed ridge regression estimator preconditioned by an affine-invariant calibrated covariance estimator achieving excess risk governed by effective degrees of freedom df_lambda(S) under fourth-moment conditions.

AIO:LinearRegression represents linear regression broadly, whereas this concept addresses random-design linear prediction and covariance preconditioning under heavy-tailed fourth-moment design and response distributions.

limitations: Sample-Splitting Logarithmic Factor in Critical Sample Size and Lack of RKHS Extension: Because Algorithm 1 splits the first half of the sample across q = ceil(log_2(L/lambda)) + 1 dyadic regularization halving stages, the critical sample size in Theorem 7 and Corollary 8 carries a logarithmic factor O(kappa^4 log(L/lambda) df_lambda(S) log(d log(L/lambda)/delta)) even though the final estimation error bound uses the unsplit second half of size r >= n/2 and avoids the q factor. Furthermore, the matrix Bernstein concentration bounds depend logarithmically on the ambient dimension d (Remark 4), leaving infinite-dimensional reproducing kernel Hilbert space (RKHS) extensions open (Section 1.2).

Requirement of Fourth-Moment Kurtosis Equivalence and Initial Spectral Norm Bound L >= ||S||: The calibrated Loewner-order guarantees require directional fourth-moment equivalence E^{1/4}[<X, u>^4] <= kappa E^{1/2}[<X, u>^2] uniformly over u in R^d (excluding distributions with infinite fourth moments) and an initial upper bound L >= ||S|| to initialize the dyadic halving schedule lambda_0 = L.

Primary-Source Typographical Notes in Ostrovskii & Rudi (2019, COLT PMLR 99:2531-2550, arXiv:1902.03086v2): Verified five minor typographical/notational details in the published manuscript: (1) Abstract (p. 1) and Section 1 (p. 2) print 'statistically interesing regime' instead of 'statistically interesting regime'; (2) Section 2.1 (p. 3) prints 'Goldon-Thompson inequality' instead of 'Golden-Thompson inequality'; (3) Section 2.3 (p. 5) prints 'asymtptocially minimax-optimal' instead of 'asymptotically minimax-optimal'; (4) Section 5 (pp. 10-11) prints 'Later on we will we show', 'stastistical guarantee', and 'a reasonables choice', while Appendix B (p. 16) prints 'Wei-Misnker estimator' instead of 'Wei-Minsker estimator'; and (5) Section 6.2 (p. 12, Eq. 33) writes rho_{theta_bar}(||Z_hat_i||^{1/2}) Z_hat_i where, because rho_theta(x) := psi_theta(x^2)/x^2 (Eq. 7) and Hermitian dilation psi_{theta_bar}(H(Z_hat_i)) truncates singular values ||Z_hat_i|| at theta_bar (Appendix D, p. 19, Eq. 50), passing ||Z_hat_i||^{1/2} into rho_{theta_bar}(.) is the exact algebraic device that makes rho_{theta_bar}(||Z_hat_i||^{1/2}) = psi_{theta_bar}(||Z_hat_i||) / ||Z_hat_i||.

All 20 pages of the full-text PDF of Ostrovskii & Rudi (2019, COLT PMLR 99:2531-2550, arXiv:1902.03086v2) were read. Constructed numerical checks in research/discovery/affine-invariant-heavy-tailed-covariance-estimation-boundaries.py verify (1) Lemma 14 dyadic effective-dimension doubling df_{lambda/2}(S) <= 2 df_lambda(S) and Lemma 6 similarity eigenvalue bounds [2/3, 2] and trace surrogate control, (2) Algorithm 1 calibrated relative spectral error (0.1238 vs. 1.2996 for uncalibrated Wei-Minsker clipping on an ill-conditioned heavy-tailed Student-t_5 covariance) and Algorithm 2 Lepskii adaptive selection (0.1577), and (3) Theorem 13 / Appendix D ridge regression excess-risk decomposition.

rows.definition: An unsupervised pretrained network that learns efficient codings of unlabeled data by training to ignore insignificant data and regenerate input from encoding.
A model which combines autoregression (AR), differencing (I), and moving average (MA) components. Used for analyzing and forecasting time series data.
A network that is a probabilistic graphical model representing variables and their conditional dependencies via a directed acyclic graph.
A machine learning task focused on methods that simultaneously cluster the rows and columns of a matrix to identify submatrices with coherent patterns.

names: stochastic Hopfield network with hidden units
rows.definition: A symmetrically connected network that is a type of stochastic recurrent neural network and Markov random field.
A probabilistic graphical model used to encode assumptions about the data-generating process.
A bias caused by differences between results and facts in the process of data analysis (including the source of data the estimator chose) and analysis methods.
An individual bias characterized by the tendency to prefer information that confirms existing beliefs influencing the search for interpretation of and recall of information.
A deep neural network self-supervised learning approach that learns to distinguish between similar and dissimilar data samples.

A large language model that is trained to pull semantically similar samples closer together and push dissimilar samples apart in the representation space learning high-quality features useful for downstream tasks.
A use and interpretation bias where testing many hypotheses in a dataset may yield apparent statistical significance even when results are nonsignificant.
A deep neural network that uses deconvolution for unsupervised construction of hierarchical image representations.
An unsupervised pretrained network composed of multiple layers of latent variables that learns to probabilistically reconstruct inputs and perform classification.
An autoencoder network that learns interpretable disentangled image representations through convolution and de-convolution layers trained with the stochastic gradient variational Bayes algorithm.
An unsupervised learning focused on the process of transforming data from a high-dimensional space into a lower-dimensional space while retaining meaningful properties of the original data.
A cognitive bias in which people with low ability in an area overestimate that ability. Often measured by comparing self-assessment with objective performance.
A machine learning task focused on methods that use multiple learning algorithms to achieve better predictive performance than any of the constituent algorithms alone.
A selection and sampling bias arising when testing populations do not equally represent user populations or when inappropriate performance metrics are used.
A regression analysis in which the model parameters are fixed or non-random quantities.
A mathematical function that computes x * P(X <= x) where P(X) ~ N(0 1) weighting inputs by their value rather than gating inputs by their sign as in ReLU.
A regularization layer that applies multiplicative 1-centered Gaussian noise.
A regularization layer that applies additive zero-centered Gaussian noise.
A deep neural network that learns novel classes from few samples per class, preventing catastrophic forgetting of base classes and ensuring classifier calibration.
A regression analysis that relates the linear model to the response variable via a link function and allowing the variance of each measurement to be a function of its predicted value.
An unsupervised pretrained network framework where two neural networks contest in a game to generate new data with the same statistics as the training set.
A systemic bias characterized by favoring members of one's in-group over out-group members expressed in evaluation resource allocation and other ways.
An individual bias characterized by unconscious beliefs attitudes feelings associations or stereotypes that affect information processing decision-making and actions.
A regression analysis that assigns the average of the values of k nearest neighbors to objects.
A network that is an unsupervised technique producing a low-dimensional representation of high-dimensional data preserving topological structure.
A regression analysis that performs both variable selection and regularization to enhance prediction accuracy and interpretability.
A regression analysis which approximates the solution of overdetermined systems by minimizing the sum of the squares of the residuals.
A regression analysis that is a linear approach for modeling the relationship between a scalar response and one or more explanatory variables.
A regression analysis that estimates the probability of an event occurring by modeling the log-odds of the event as a linear combination of one or more independent variables.
A network that is a stochastic model describing a sequence of possible events where the probability of each event depends only on the previous event's state.

A large language model which dynamically selects and combines outputs from multiple expert submodels, allowing for efficient scaling by conditionally activating only a subset of model components for each input.
A large language model which is trained jointly on multiple language tasks simultaneously, learning shared representations that transfer across tasks.
An activation layer that applies parametric rectified linear unit function element-wise.
A machine learning task in which a graph expresses the conditional dependence structure between random variables.
A hidden layer that estimates the probability of a sample being within a certain category.
A probabilistic graphical model that uses statistical techniques to analyze the words in each text to discover common themes their connections and their changes over time.
A regression analysis for survival analysis where the unique effect of a unit increase in a covariate is multiplicative with respect to the hazard rate.
An image preprocessing layer that randomly adjusts contrast during training.
A regression analysis where the model parameters are random variables.
An ensemble learning method for classification regression and other tasks that constructs a multitude of decision trees during training.
A set of statistical processes for estimating the relationships between a dependent variable and one or more independent variables.
A regression analysis that estimates the coefficients of multiple regression models in scenarios where the independent variables are highly correlated.
An individual bias characterized by the tendency to selectively adopt algorithmic advice that matches pre-existing beliefs and stereotypes.
A machine learning task that is intermediate between supervised and unsupervised learning and predicts parts of the input data from other observed parts without relying on human-annotated labels.
A regression analysis used to model spatial relationships.
A biclustering task focused on methods that simultaneously cluster the rows and columns of a labeled matrix considering data labels to enhance cluster coherence.
A network with supervised learning models for classification and regression that maps training examples to points in space maximizing the gap between categories.
A machine learning task focused on methods for analyzing time series data to extract meaningful statistics and characteristics.

A preprocessing used to train machine learning models including techniques such as supervised learning unsupervised learning reinforcement learning and transfer learning aimed at optimizing model performance.
A biclustering task focused on methods that simultaneously cluster the rows and columns of an unlabeled input matrix to identify submatrices with coherent patterns.
A clustering focused on methods that group a set of unlabeled objects such that objects in the same group are more similar to each other than to those in other groups.
A large language model that is trained solely on unlabeled data using self-supervised objectives like masked language modeling without any supervised fine-tuning.
A machine learning task focused on algorithms that learn patterns from unlabeled data.
A network that initializes a discriminative neural net from one trained using an unsupervised criterion.
An autoencoder network that imposes a probabilistic structure on the latent space for unsupervised learning.

A model that captures the linear interdependencies among multiple time series, where each variable is modeled as a linear function of its own past values and the past values of all other variables in the system.
A dimensionality reduction for visualizing high-dimensional data by giving each datapoint a location in a two or three-dimensional map.

native_neighbors.name: Adafactor
native_neighbors.definition: An adaptive gradient optimization method that approximates matrix-valued second-moment statistics using row and column factors.

native_neighbors.name: Adam
native_neighbors.definition: Stochastic gradient optimization using bias-corrected exponential estimates of first and second gradient moments to scale parameter updates.

native_neighbors.name: Adaptive Metropolis
native_neighbors.definition: A history-adaptive random-walk Metropolis sampler whose Gaussian proposal covariance is estimated from the accumulated retained states, including repetitions after rejected proposals.

native_neighbors.name: Adaptive parallel tempering
native_neighbors.definition: A parallel-tempering algorithm that adapts temperature gaps and within-replica random-walk proposal parameters through projected stochastic approximation.

native_neighbors.name: Adaptive rejection sampling
native_neighbors.definition: The Gilks–Wild univariate rejection sampler that uses tangents to a concave log density as a piecewise-linear upper hull and chords as a lower hull, updating these bounds from evaluated proposals.

native_neighbors.name: Adaptive scaling Metropolis
native_neighbors.definition: A random-walk Metropolis algorithm that adapts its proposal scale through stochastic approximation driven by the proposal acceptance probability relative to a chosen target rate.

native_neighbors.name: Admixture of Poisson Markov random fields
native_neighbors.definition: A probabilistic topic-model family that draws each document from a proper Poisson-MRF base distribution whose canonical unary and interaction parameters are convex combinations of topic parameters under document-specific simplex weights.

native_neighbors.name: Analytic moment-based Gaussian-process filtering
native_neighbors.definition: A Gaussian assumed-density filtering algorithm that uses trained squared-exponential Gaussian-process transition and measurement models, analytically matches predictive moments under Gaussian state inputs, and conditions a moment-matched Gaussian approximation to the joint state/measurement distribution to update the hidden-state estimate.

native_neighbors.name: Ancestral Gumbel-Top-k sampling
native_neighbors.definition: An exact without-replacement sampler for finite discrete Bayesian-network configurations that propagates conditional Gumbel subtree maxima through a bounded priority frontier, with a configurable number of parallel expansions and parent-respecting variable selection.

native_neighbors.name: AntNet
native_neighbors.definition: A distributed adaptive routing algorithm in which forward agents sample network paths and backward agents use the measured trip times to update local traffic models and probabilistic routing tables.

native_neighbors.name: Asynchronous Successive Halving
native_neighbors.definition: An asynchronous resource-allocation algorithm that promotes promising completed hyperparameter trials through increasing resource levels as workers become available and starts new trials when no eligible promotion is available, without waiting for an entire evaluation stage to finish.

native_neighbors.name: Attention-based Dropout Layer
native_neighbors.definition: A training-time convolutional feature-map layer that stochastically applies either a thresholded spatial drop mask or sigmoid importance weights derived from channel-averaged activations, developed for weakly supervised object localization.

native_neighbors.name: Author-persona-topic model
native_neighbors.definition: A probabilistic topic-model family in which each author has a mixture of personas, each persona has a topic distribution, and one persona shared across a document generates its token topics.

native_neighbors.name: Auto-normal Markov random field
native_neighbors.definition: A proper finite Gaussian Markov-field model specified by linear full-conditional means and positive, value-independent site conditional variances, with compatibility enforced by a symmetric positive-definite joint precision matrix.

native_neighbors.name: Averaged stochastic gradient descent
native_neighbors.definition: A stochastic gradient optimization method that maintains an average of parameter iterates in addition to the current iterate.

native_neighbors.name: BOHB
native_neighbors.definition: A hyperparameter optimization algorithm combining Hyperband resource brackets with model-guided configuration proposals from performance-split multivariate kernel density estimates and a continuing random-sampling component.

native_neighbors.name: Barber–Agakov mutual information bound
native_neighbors.definition: A variational lower bound on mutual information formed by adding input entropy to the expected log probability assigned by a normalized conditional decoder to the input given the output.

native_neighbors.name: Bayesian Data Augmentation for Deep Models
native_neighbors.definition: Tran et al.’s supervised deep-learning procedure that treats synthetic labeled examples as latent data, repeatedly samples them from an evolving learned model and updates model parameters through a generalized Monte Carlo expectation-maximization formulation.

native_neighbors.name: Beam-stack search
native_neighbors.definition: A layer-based beam search augmented with a stack of admitted evaluation ranges so that backtracking systematically revisits successors previously discarded by beam-width pruning.

native_neighbors.name: Best-first search
native_neighbors.definition: A search strategy that repeatedly expands the open node with the best value under a specified evaluation rule, adding eligible successors to the open frontier.

native_neighbors.name: Binary Multiple Kernel Maximum Margin Clustering
native_neighbors.definition: A two-class unsupervised clustering procedure that jointly fits a nonnegative multiple-kernel combination and absolute-margin classifier using cutting-plane constraints and constrained concave-convex updates.

native_neighbors.name: Black box variational inference
native_neighbors.definition: A variational-inference procedure that estimates evidence-lower-bound gradients from samples of a tractable variational distribution using its score function and model log joint, with mean-field local signals and score control variates to manage estimator variance.

native_neighbors.name: Bootstrap classifier-instability novelty detection
native_neighbors.definition: A novelty-detection procedure that trains classifiers on bootstrap resamples of reference data, estimates the variance of their outputs at a query, and rejects queries with unusually high variability relative to a chosen reference-score threshold.

native_neighbors.name: CART
native_neighbors.definition: Decision-tree induction using binary recursive partitioning for classification or regression.

native_neighbors.name: CD-PercLoss
native_neighbors.definition: A conditional RBM training algorithm that contrasts the observed output free energy with that of a prediction selected by input-initialized stochastic search, treating the selected prediction as fixed during differentiation.

native_neighbors.name: CHAMELEON clustering
native_neighbors.definition: A graph-clustering procedure that first partitions a sparse neighbor graph into small subclusters and then agglomerates them using interconnectivity and closeness normalized by their internal bisection statistics.

native_neighbors.name: Classification Annealing Expectation Maximization
native_neighbors.definition: A stochastic hard-clustering algorithm that samples component assignments from current mixture posterior probabilities raised to an inverse positive temperature, maximizes the completed-data classification likelihood, and lowers the temperature according to a chosen schedule.

native_neighbors.name: Classification Expectation Maximization
native_neighbors.definition: A model-based hard-clustering algorithm that computes mixture responsibilities, assigns every observation to a highest-responsibility component, and maximizes the completed-data classification likelihood for that assignment.

native_neighbors.name: Clustering Data by Melting
native_neighbors.definition: A scale-dependent clustering procedure that heats Gaussian-weighted center iterations to build a merging membership tree, then selects clusters by persistence of their within-cluster weight fraction across logarithmic scales.

native_neighbors.name: Composite HMM-topic model
native_neighbors.definition: A generative sequence model combining an HMM class sequence with a document topic mixture, where one designated class emits words through latent topics and each other class emits words from its own categorical distribution.

native_neighbors.name: Consistency model
native_neighbors.definition: A generative model family that learns a noise- or time-conditioned function mapping points on a probability-flow ODE trajectory to its common low-noise endpoint, enabling a sample to be obtained with one model evaluation and allowing optional multistep refinement.

native_neighbors.name: Contrastive divergence
native_neighbors.definition: A parameter-learning algorithm for energy-based or product-of-experts models that replaces the equilibrium negative-phase expectation by configurations obtained from a short model-invariant Markov chain restarted at observed data, without differentiating through the chain distribution.

native_neighbors.name: Contrastive predictive coding
native_neighbors.definition: A representation-learning procedure that encodes observations, summarizes preceding representations as context, and jointly trains these components to distinguish future representations from sampled alternatives using InfoNCE.

native_neighbors.name: Global Kernel K-Means with Convex Mixture Models
native_neighbors.definition: An incremental kernel clustering algorithm that fits a convex mixture over datum exemplars once, restricts each new-cluster seed search to its selected high-weight exemplars, and retains the lowest-error local kernel k-means fit.

native_neighbors.name: Core-set support vector data description
native_neighbors.definition: An approximate one-class training algorithm that grows a core subset using the nearest expanded-sphere violator, refits support vector data description and enforces radius growth until the expanded sphere meets an outlier-count stopping rule.

native_neighbors.name: Core vector regression
native_neighbors.definition: A support-vector regression training algorithm that approximates a penalized-bias, paired squared-slack formulation with a learned unconstrained margin using a center-constrained minimum enclosing ball over two transformed points per observation.

native_neighbors.name: Correlation-based Hammerstein identification
native_neighbors.definition: A two-stage identification algorithm for a real-valued single-input single-output polynomial Hammerstein cascade that estimates a scaled linear response from Gaussian-excited input/output cross-correlation, then fits the input polynomial by least squares on filtered input powers.

native_neighbors.name: Correlation-based Wiener identification
native_neighbors.definition: A two-stage identification algorithm for a real-valued single-input single-output polynomial Wiener cascade that estimates a scaled linear response from Gaussian-excited input/output cross-correlation, then fits the output polynomial by least squares on the reconstructed internal signal.

native_neighbors.name: Crank–Nicolson Langevin sampling
native_neighbors.definition: A Metropolis-corrected Gaussian-reference sampler that combines a Crank–Nicolson treatment of the reference precision with an explicit gradient drift of the remaining target potential.

native_neighbors.name: Crank–Nicolson Metropolis sampling
native_neighbors.definition: A Metropolis sampler for a Gaussian-reference target using a Crank–Nicolson discretization of the unpreconditioned reference Ornstein–Uhlenbeck dynamics as its proposal.

native_neighbors.name: Cross-entropy optimization
native_neighbors.definition: A stochastic optimization method that iteratively samples a parameterized search distribution, selects high-performing samples using an adaptive threshold, and refits the distribution by maximum likelihood on those selected samples.

native_neighbors.name: Cross-validated prior-likelihood conflict diagnostic
native_neighbors.definition: A Bayesian hierarchical-model diagnostic that leaves an assessed unit out of population-parameter fitting, generates predictive-prior and reference-prior likelihood replicates of its unit effect, and measures their signed conflict under an explicitly specified replication law. Shared nuisance parameters require controlled feedback and dependence handling.

native_neighbors.name: DEHB
native_neighbors.definition: A hyperparameter optimization algorithm that combines Hyperband resource schedules with differential-evolution populations at different resource levels, using promising lower-resource configurations to guide proposals evaluated and selected at higher resource levels.

native_neighbors.name: DINO self-distillation
native_neighbors.definition: A self-supervised representation-learning procedure that matches cross-view student probabilities to centered and sharpened probabilities from a momentum teacher, without a separate prediction head or explicit negative-pair objective.

native_neighbors.name: Deep autoregressive network
